node_definition.done_when:
Two test-suite hygiene defects, both measured on this workstation on 2026-10-03.

1. Temporary directories are never cleaned. pytest 9.1 defaults tmp_path_retention_policy to "all", and the [tool.pytest.ini_options] block in pyproject.toml sets only `timeout`. Every test's tmp_path therefore survives the run. Four coordinator population runs with explicit per-arm --basetemp left 5.2 GB on the fleet node's /tmp, which reached 90%. Worker gates and whole-suite runs accumulate the same way. Set tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed" in pyproject.toml, with a one-line comment giving the reason, so that only failed tests keep their directories for debugging. Measure it: run a fixed sample of about 20 test files twice with an explicit --basetemp, before and after the change, and record the basetemp's size after each run (du -sk) in docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/suite-cleans-its-temp.html.
2. The live-Jev guard rests only on the credential being absent. tests/conftest.py's no_live_jev fixture removes OPENROUTER_API_KEY_RECKON and points the credential at an absent path. A test that sets the key itself would still reach OpenRouter. In the same autouse fixture, stub the client's HTTP call (urllib.request.urlopen as reckon/crew/picker/client.py uses it, or the client's own post function) so that it raises the existing LiveJevDisabled error whatever the credential. Tests that mock the call themselves must keep working. Add a case to tests/test_suite_never_calls_live_jev.py that sets a fake key, dispatches a dry run with no lane named, and asserts that no network call was attempted and that the selection is a recorded fallback. Deleting the HTTP stub must make that case fail; that is the negative control.

Gate: tests/test_suite_never_calls_live_jev.py, tests/test_picker*.py and a 20-file sample including tests/test_capabilities.py and tests/test_dispatch_speed.py. Run them with the main checkout's .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 in the FOREGROUND, with one log for base and one for head under the run directory, each ending in an EXIT line, judged by delta.
